why: The criterion holds for all four checks. Check 1 only asserts that clamp is exported and returns the clamped value: inside the range, below it, above it, at each bound, lo === hi via clamp(3,3,3), and decimals. The words force all of these, since lo === hi is not "lo greater than hi" and a range of 3 to 3 still returns 3. Check 2 passes or fails only on whether a RangeError is thrown when lo > hi. Check 3 runs a heading script, but its PASS condition falls back to judging "whether that function is actually documented", so no exact heading format is required. Check 4 needs only an exit code of 0 with no failing tests. The stricter items (clamp tests in the test file, the RangeError mention in README) are under "Advisory". One flaw: the Advisory list includes clamp(2,2,2), which Check 1 already enforces with clamp(3,3,3). That is redundant, not a requirement beyond the words.
